name: onlycat-dfm
description: Injection moulding design-for-manufacture analyser — single-file browser tool

scripts.test:smoke: node build.js && node test/make-fixtures.mjs && node test/smoke.mjs
scripts.test:offline: node build.js --vendor && node test/make-fixtures.mjs && node test/offline.mjs && node build.js
scripts.test: node build.js && node test/unit.mjs && node test/make-fixtures.mjs && node test/smoke.mjs

comments.devDependencies: None of these are shipped. dfm-tool.html loads three.js and jsPDF from a CDN at runtime; the smoke test serves these local copies in their place so it never touches the network. playwright drives the browser it runs in.
comments.browser: npm install fetches the playwright library but not the browser binary. Run `npm run browser` once after installing, or set DFM_CHROMIUM to a Chromium you already have.
comments.build:offline: Inlines three.js and jsPDF so the output needs no network at all — about 1.4 MB instead of 500 kB. The committed deliverable is the CDN-loading one; this is for handing someone a file that has to work on a machine with no internet.
comments.test:offline: Builds the vendored output, proves it runs with every off-origin request refused, then rebuilds the normal one so the tree is left as it was found.
comments.verify:build: dfm-tool.html is the deliverable and is committed. Rebuilds and fails if the result differs from the committed copy, which a source-only commit would otherwise leave stale. Assumes a clean working tree, so it is a CI check rather than a pre-commit one — with src/ edits in progress it will fail by design.
